extracted.intended_audience: unemployed younger sons of the nobility; gentlemen considering new professions
extracted.subtask_description: Advice (satirical but prescriptive) on how a gentleman could practice auctioneering with dignity and profit — aimed at aristocratic men seeking a respectable new profession. The text lists qualities to cultivate, things to avoid, and what stock/categories suit a 'genteel' auctioneer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gentlemanly birth and fashion
rubrics_metrics.description: The auctioneer should be 'a man of first-rate and irreproachable birth and fashion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a person will attract the best society to his 'pulpit' and his presence will make attendance a privilege; only a person of high breeding can supply the refining social cachet the role requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refined appearance and agreeable person
rubrics_metrics.description: He should be so agreeable in person that 'it must be a pleasure for ladies to behold and tailors to dress it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pleasing person and well-dressed appearance encourage trust and attendance; physical bearing and dress are part of the professional appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Move in the best society / strong social connections
rubrics_metrics.description: He 'must move in the very best society, which will flock round his pulpit when he mounts it in his public calling.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-society contacts both provide clients and signal to buyers that the sale is for tasteful, valuable objects — attracting the genteel clientele needed for high prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of art, literature, and taste
rubrics_metrics.description: The auctioneer 'must have a good knowledge of the history and language of all nations' and be 'elegantly conversant' with lighter literature, pictures, bindings, china, jewelry, arms, and antiquities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He should be able to give neat histories of authors, speak convincingly about galleries and binding, and eloquently contextualize pictures/antiques to entice buyers; avoid heavy antiquarian or philological works but handle tasteful items expertly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate tact and conversational skill
rubrics_metrics.description: He must 'have the tact only acquired in good society, and know where a joke is in place, and how far a compliment may go.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use praise, wit, and anecdote judiciously so as to amuse and flatter clients without offending them; familiarity or crude banter will repel refined buyers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty and sincerity
rubrics_metrics.description: The auctioneer 'must not sacrifice his honesty ... nor tell fibs about himself or them' and must have 'a character of sincerity to support.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not misrepresent goods (e.g., call a copy a Raffaelle); the public is your client as much as the seller, and long-term trust is essential to success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vulgarity, pomposity, and affectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the 'swaggering quackery' and 'Bartholomew-fair advocacy' of vulgar auctioneers; do not ape titles or use pompous self-descriptions (e.g., 'representative').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use loud, vulgar trumpeting or excessive bravado in adverts or in the room; also avoid grandiose job-titles or calling the room a 'study' — prefer modest terms like 'private room' or 'office.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion in praise (selective eulogizing)
rubrics_metrics.description: He 'will not outrageously and indiscriminately laud all objects committed to his charge, for he knows the value of praise.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise should be measured and credible; indiscriminate lauding cheapens both the auctioneer and the goods, deterring discerning buyers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine enthusiasm and feeling for objects
rubrics_metrics.description: He 'must feel them' and be 'a glass in which all the tastes of fashion are reflected' — not merely affect enthusiasm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentic appreciation for books, porcelain, jewelry, arms, etc., will carry conviction; affected appreciation is transparent and ineffective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eloquence and oratorical skill suited to auctioneering
rubrics_metrics.description: His 'pulpit oratory' should be 'invaluable' — able to speak engagingly and draw listeners in (even 'out of a single teacup cause streams of world-philosophy to flow').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate lively, tasteful rhetoric that makes objects compelling to buyers without vulgar exaggeration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tasteful choice of inventory (focus on tasteful/taste-sensitive goods)
rubrics_metrics.description: He should not sell lowly practical goods (pigs, ploughs, cart-horses, public-house goodwill) but 'all articles properly called of taste' — pictures, china, jewelry, gold-headed canes, valuable arms, picturesque antiquities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the stock to items that require refined judgment and appeal to genteel buyers; certain classes of merchandise are unsuitable for a 'genteel' auctioneer's reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ostentatious, vulgar advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: The common loud advertising ('vulgar trumpeting' and 'Bartholomew-fair advocacy') is a mistake; it keeps refined people away and signals cheapness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a refined publicity style; excessive shouting or sensational promotion can depress perceived value and attendance among the target clientele.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of appropriate limits (when not to deal)
rubrics_metrics.description: He should refrain from handling 'heavy antiquarian and philological works' and other categories where a lighter, fashionable touch is ineffective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize which classes of goods suit your persona and expertise; avoid items that require specialist scholarly knowledge beyond the 'genteel' auctioneer's remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of office and terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid grand or vulgar terms for rooms and roles ('study', 'representative'); prefer 'private room' or 'office' and be simply an 'auctioneer' rather than an 'advocate'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use modest, appropriate professional language that conveys dignity without pretension; terminology influences perception of sincerity and standing.
